## Summary This change only touches the frontend. The four board columns (Unplanned, Planned, AI queue, Finished) are currently rendered side by side in a 4‑column grid in `patchgoblin/templates/index.html` and filled by `renderBoard()` in `patchgoblin/static/app.js` (lines 157–164). I'll replace that with a tab bar that has one tab per queue, and only the active queue's card list will be visible. Following your feedback, each tab's badge counts **only actionable tasks**. An actionable task is one the user can still act on: it isn't locked by the AI and isn't finished. This follows the backend's own rule, `LOCKED = ("planning", "running")` in `patchgoblin/app.py:17`. So `ACTIONABLE = {unplanned, planned, queued, failed}`, and `planning`, `running` and `done` are not counted. Per tab, that gives: | Tab | Counts | Not counted | |---|---|---| | Unplanned | `unplanned` | `planning` | | Planned | `planned` | — | | AI queue | `queued` (can still be edited or removed from the queue) | `running` | | Finished | `failed` | `done` | Non-actionable tasks are still listed in the tab's panel. They just don't add to the badge. So the user can still tell the AI is busy, a small activity dot appears on a tab while it holds a `planning` or `running` task. A tooltip on each tab gives the full breakdown. The active tab is stored in `state` and saved to `localStorage`, the same way `pg.pid` is. `renderBoard()` already runs on every 3‑second poll, so the badges stay up to date without backend changes. The tabs use `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`/`role="tabpanel"` markup and support arrow-key navigation. ## Steps 1. **`patchgoblin/templates/index.html` (lines 59–64)** - Add a tab bar above `.board`: ```html
… planned / queue ("AI queue") / finished …
``` - Keep the four `.column` divs but give each one `id="col-"`, `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby="tab-"`. - Remove the `

` header and its `.count` from each column. The tab now does that job. 2. **`app.js`: constants and state (lines 6–22)** - Add `const ACTIONABLE = new Set(["unplanned", "planned", "queued", "failed"]);` next to `COLUMN_OF`, with a one-line comment: "not locked by the AI and not finished; mirrors LOCKED in app.py". - Add `const BUSY = new Set(["planning", "running"]);`. - Add `tab: validTab(localStorageGet("pg.tab"))` to `state`. `validTab` returns the stored value if it's one of `Object.values(COLUMN_OF)`, and `"unplanned"` otherwise. 3. **`app.js`: `renderBoard()` (line 157)** - Keep the per-column filter, sort and card fill. - For each column, work out: - `actionable = tasks.filter(t => ACTIONABLE.has(t.status)).length` - `busy = tasks.some(t => BUSY.has(t.status))` - Update the matching `.queue-tab[data-col=…]`: - Set `.count` text to `actionable || ""`, and toggle the `empty` class so the pill is hidden at 0. - Set `.activity.hidden = !busy`. - Set `title` and `aria-label` to the full breakdown, e.g. `"AI queue: 2 actionable, 1 running (3 total)"`. Build the parts from the `STATUS_LABEL` counts so screen readers and hover give the complete picture. - Set `aria-selected`, the `active` class and `tabindex` (`0` for the active tab, `-1` for the others). - Set `column.hidden = col !== state.tab`. - If the visible panel has no tasks, show an empty-state line inside `.cards`, e.g. `el("div", { class: "muted empty-col" }, "No tasks here")`. 4. **`app.js`: add `selectTab(col, focus = false)`** - Set `state.tab = col`, call `localStorageSet("pg.tab", col)` and then `renderBoard()`. If `focus` is true, focus the tab button. - In the init/wiring section (around line 603), add: - a click handler on each `.queue-tab` that calls `selectTab(btn.dataset.col)`; - a `keydown` handler on `.queue-tabs`. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move to the neighbouring tab with wrap-around, Home/End jump to the first/last tab, and each calls `selectTab(next, true)`. 5. **`app.js`: `createTask()` (line 185)** - After a successful create, call `selectTab("unplanned")` if a different tab is active, so the new card is visible. 6. **Drawer actions and polling (around lines 247–340)** - Don't change the tab automatically when a task changes status, whether from a drawer action or the 3‑second poll. The open drawer still shows the task, and the badges and activity dot show where it went. 7. **`patchgoblin/static/app.css`, board section (around lines 152–157, media query around line 275)** - Change `.board` from a 4‑column grid to a single block, with `.column` at full width. - Add `.column[hidden] { display: none; }`, the same pattern the file uses for `.drawer[hidden]` and `.row[hidden]`. - `.queue-tabs`: a flex row with a bottom border and a gap, and `overflow-x: auto` for narrow screens. - `.queue-tab`: ghost-button style. `.active` gets an accent underline plus stronger text, and there's a `:focus-visible` outline. - `.queue-tab .count`: a pill in the accent colour. `.count.empty { display: none; }`. - `.queue-tab .activity`: a small pulsing dot. Reuse the running badge colour and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - `.column .cards`: `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(260px, 1fr)); gap: …`, so one full-width panel doesn't show a single narrow stack of cards. - Remove the `.board { grid-template-columns: 1fr }` override from the mobile media query. 8. **`README.md`**: if it describes the four-column board, change it to say "tabbed queues; badges show actionable tasks". ## Verification - Run `uv run pytest`. Add one test to `tests/test_patchgoblin.py` that GETs `/` and checks that the four `role="tab"` buttons with `data-col` values `unplanned`, `planned`, `queue` and `finished` are present, and that each `.column` has a matching `role="tabpanel"`. - Manual check with `uv run python run.py` (or the `run` skill): - Only one queue is visible at a time, and clicking a tab switches the panel. - Adding a task switches to Unplanned and increases its badge by 1. - Start AI planning. The Unplanned badge drops by 1 while it's `planning` and the activity dot shows. When planning finishes, the Planned badge increases. - Queue a task for AI. The AI queue badge increases. When the task starts `running`, the badge drops and the dot shows. On `done`, the Finished badge doesn't change. On `failed`, it increases. - When a tab has 0 actionable tasks, its pill is hidden. The tooltip and `aria-label` still give the full breakdown. - Reloading keeps the selected tab. Switching projects keeps the tab, and the badges update. - ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End move between tabs and focus follows the selected tab. - At mobile width the tab bar scrolls horizontally. - If the drawer is open, switching tabs doesn't close or break it. ## Open questions and risks - **Should `queued` count as actionable?** I've counted it because the backend lets the user still edit a queued task or remove it from the queue. If you'd rather it meant "needs my attention now", drop `queued` from `ACTIONABLE`. The AI queue badge would then usually be empty, and the activity dot would be its only signal. It's a one-line change to the constant. - **Should `done` ever count?** If finished tasks need a human review or sign-off, `done` should count until that happens. That would need a new "reviewed" flag in the backend, which is out of scope here. - **Should the tab be remembered globally or per project?** The plan uses a single global `pg.tab`. Per project would use a key like `pg.tab.`. - **Risk:** `tests/browser-smoke.cjs` is deleted in the working tree. If it's restored, any `.column h3 .count` selectors in it will need updating.

# Plan: Task #2 — batch actions (revised)

## Summary
Add one batch endpoint that runs any per-task action on a list of task ids. It reuses the same rules as the existing single-task `/action` route, so a batch can't do anything a single click can't. Each task succeeds or fails on its own: a bad id is reported and the rest still go through.

On the board, each card gets a checkbox. Once something is selected, a batch toolbar appears in the current tab, showing only the actions that fit the selected tasks' statuses. Selection stays within the current tab. The actions are **Plan with AI**, **Mark planned**, **Queue for AI**, **Remove from queue**, **Back to unplanned**, **Reopen**, **Cancel**, **Delete** and **Set provider**.

Following your feedback, planning concurrency is now a **per-project** setting, `plan_limit`. It sits on the project record next to `provider`/`model` and can be edited from the project bar. **By default there is no limit**, so today's behaviour is unchanged unless you set one. Batch-queued tasks run in id order.

## Steps

1. **Pull the single-task logic into a shared helper** (`patchgoblin/app.py`)
   - Move the body of `task_action` (plan / cancel / `TRANSITIONS`) into a local helper, `apply_action(project, tid, action, data) -> None`.
     - It raises `ValueError`/`LookupError` as the route does today, and doesn't call `engine.kick`.
     - Inside it, replace `find_task(...) or abort(404)` with `raise KeyError(tid)`.
   - `task_action` calls `apply_action`, turns a `KeyError` into a 404, calls `engine.kick(pid)` for `queue`, and returns `task_view` as it does now. Its behaviour doesn't change.

2. **Add the batch route** (`patchgoblin/app.py`)
   - `POST /api/projects/<pid>/tasks/batch` with body `{action, ids: [int], feedback?, provider?}`.
   - Validation: `ids` must be a non-empty list of ints (de-duplicated, capped at 200), and `action` must be in `TRANSITIONS ∪ {"plan", "cancel", "delete", "set_provider"}`. Anything else is a 400.
   - **Status changes** (`mark_planned`, `unplan`, `queue`, `dequeue`, `reopen`):
     - Do them all inside **one** `store.edit(project)`, so SSH projects get one read and one write.
     - Skip tasks in the wrong status and record why.
     - For `queue`, give every task the same `now()`. `_claim` sorts by `(queued_at, id)`, so the batch runs in id order.
     - Call `engine.kick(pid)` once at the end.
   - **`plan`**: loop `engine.start_planning(project, tid, feedback)`, catching `ValueError`/`KeyError` for each task.
   - **`cancel`**: loop `engine.cancel(pid, tid)` for each task.
   - **`delete`**: one `store.edit`, skipping `LOCKED` tasks (the same rule as `delete_task`).
   - **`set_provider`**: one `store.edit`.
     - Check the provider against `PROVIDERS`; `""` means the project default.
     - Skip locked tasks.
     - Call `log_event(task, "Edited provider")`.
   - Response: `{"results": [{"id", "ok", "error"?}], "tasks": [task_view(...)...]}`, built from `store.read(project, fresh=True)`. It always returns 200; failures for individual tasks are reported in `results`.

3. **Per-project planning limit, unlimited by default** (`patchgoblin/app.py`, `patchgoblin/engine.py`)
   - **`update_project`**: accept `plan_limit`.
     - `null`, `""` or `0` means unlimited and is stored as `0`.
     - A positive int is stored as is.
     - Anything else raises `ValueError("Plan limit must be a whole number ≥ 0.")`.
     - Existing projects have no key, which is read as `0`, so no migration is needed.
   - **`Engine`**: add a per-project gate, `self._plan_gates: dict[str, threading.Condition]`, plus a count of active planners per project.
     - In `_plan`, before `self._ai(...)`, wait while `limit > 0 and active >= limit`. Read the limit from `self.registry.get(pid)` on every check so a change takes effect without a restart.
     - Increment the count on entry and decrement it in `finally`, then call `notify_all()`.
     - Use `wait(timeout=1)` so the loop can check `job.cancelled` and raise `Cancelled` before any AI process starts.
     - I'm using a Condition instead of a Semaphore because the limit can change at runtime and `0` must mean "no gate".
   - A task waiting for a slot stays in the "Planning…" state. Optionally it can add one log line, "Waiting for a planning slot".

4. **Project-bar control** (`patchgoblin/templates/index.html`, `patchgoblin/static/app.js`)
   - Next to `#p-provider`/`#p-model`, add `<input id="p-plan-limit" type="number" min="0" placeholder="∞" title="Max simultaneous planning jobs (blank = unlimited)">`.
   - In the function that fills `#p-provider` (around `app.js:151`), set it to `p.plan_limit || ""`.
   - Its `onchange` calls `updateProject({ plan_limit: e.target.value === "" ? 0 : Number(e.target.value) })`, the same way `#p-model` does.

5. **Selection state and batch toolbar** (`patchgoblin/static/app.js`)
   - **Selection state**
     - Add `state.selected = new Set()` and `state.lastSelected`.
     - Clear them in `selectProject` and `selectTab`.
     - In `renderBoard`, prune ids that are no longer in the current tab.
   - **`renderCard`**
     - Add a leading checkbox. Its click handler calls `stopPropagation()` so ticking doesn't open the drawer.
     - Shift-click selects a range in the column's sorted order.
     - Add a `.selected` class to ticked cards.
   - **`renderBatchBar()`**, called from `renderBoard`:
     - It shows "N selected", select-all/none for the current tab, and the action buttons.
     - Keep a `BATCH_ACTIONS` table of `{label, fromStatuses}`, mirroring the drawer's `switch`.
     - A button is shown when at least one selected task qualifies, labelled with the count ("Queue 4 for AI").
     - Set provider: a `#batch-provider` select plus an Apply button.
   - **`doBatch(action, extra)`**
     - Confirm before `delete`/`cancel`.
     - For `plan`, `prompt()` for optional shared feedback.
     - POST, then replace `state.tasks` with `data.tasks`.
     - Toast a summary, e.g. "Queued 4, skipped 1: #7 is running".
     - Clear the ids that succeeded from the selection.
     - Re-render the open drawer only if its task was affected and `!state.dirty`. If the drawer has unsaved edits, leave it alone and mention that in the toast.
   - **Keyboard**: Space toggles a focused card; Escape clears the selection when neither the drawer nor the chat panel is open.

6. **Markup and styles** (`patchgoblin/templates/index.html`, `patchgoblin/static/app.css`)
   - Add `<div id="batch-bar" class="batch-bar" hidden role="toolbar" aria-label="Batch actions">` between `.queue-tabs` and `.board`, with `#batch-provider` filled from the `providers` template variable.
   - Styles: a sticky bar, a checkbox that doesn't change card height, and a highlighted `.card.selected`. Size the width of `#p-plan-limit` to fit.

7. **Docs** (`README.md`): add a "Batch actions" section and a note about the project's "Plan limit" (blank means unlimited).

## Verification
- **New tests in `tests/test_patchgoblin.py`** (`WorkflowTests`, using `add_project`, `post_task`, `wait_for`):
  - `test_batch_mark_planned_and_queue`: 3 tasks go to planned, then are queued with `engine.kick` mocked. All three become `queued` with the same `queued_at`, and `kick` is called once.
  - `test_batch_partial_failure`: unplanned, planned and missing ids with action `queue`. Only the planned tasks succeed, and the response is 200.
  - `test_batch_plan_unlimited`: batch plan on 3 tasks with the default `plan_limit` and `fake_agent.py`. All reach `planned`.
  - `test_batch_plan_respects_limit`: PATCH the project with `plan_limit: 1`, use a slow fake agent (or wrap `engine._ai` to record concurrent entries), and check that the peak concurrency is 1. All tasks still reach `planned`.
  - `test_plan_limit_validation`: `-1` and `"abc"` give 400; `0` and `""` are stored as `0`.
  - `test_batch_cancel_waiting_planner`: with `plan_limit: 1`, cancel the task that is waiting for a slot. It goes back to its previous status, and its AI process never starts.
  - `test_batch_delete_skips_locked` and `test_batch_validation`: a bad action, empty ids and non-int ids give 400; a request without the `X-PatchGoblin` header gives 403.
  - The existing single-action tests must still pass without changes.
- **Run:** `python -m unittest tests.test_patchgoblin -v`
- **Manual check** (`python -m patchgoblin`):
  - Batch-plan 5 Unplanned tasks: all start at once. Set Plan limit to 2 and repeat: only 2 run at a time.
  - Batch-queue from Planned: tasks run in id order.
  - Shift-click range selection works.
  - Selection survives the 3-second auto-refresh.
  - Ticking a checkbox doesn't open the drawer.

## Risks
- **Unlimited is the default**, so batch-planning many tasks can launch many CLI processes at once and hit provider rate limits. The README and the input tooltip should point to the setting.
- **Cancelling a waiting planner**: `Job.cancelled` must be checked inside the wait loop, not only once the slot is free, or cancelled tasks will sit waiting.
- **Lowering the limit** while jobs are running doesn't stop them; it only holds back new ones. That's intended, but it shouldn't look like a bug.
- **Uncommitted changes**: `app.py`/`store.py` may have uncommitted working-tree changes. Apply the refactor on top of those, not on top of HEAD.
- **Auto-refresh**: a refresh can re-render the board mid-click. Selection has to live in `state`, not the DOM.
- **Failed tasks**: batch "Plan with AI" on a Failed task sends it back to its previous status, the same as the single-task action does today.

## Questions for you
None.

# Plan for task #4: optionally rewrite the task title when the AI finishes planning

## Summary
Add a per-project boolean, `rewrite_titles`, to the project records in the registry (`projects.json`). It defaults to on: a project without the field is treated as `True`. When it's on, `plan_prompt` asks the AI to start its reply with one line, `Title: <concise title>`, followed by the plan. When a plan succeeds, `Engine._plan` removes that line from the output, stores the rest as the plan, and replaces the task title if the new one is non-empty and different. It also adds a history entry recording the old title. If the AI leaves out the line, the plan is stored unchanged and the title stays as it is. The setting is a checkbox in the project controls bar, saved through the existing `PATCH /api/projects/<pid>` route. Only AI planning is affected. The manual `mark_planned` action has no AI involved and keeps the title. Task titles can't be edited while a task is `planning` (`LOCKED`), so the rename can't overwrite an edit the user made in the meantime.

## Steps
1. **`patchgoblin/providers.py`**
   - Add a `TITLE_INSTRUCTIONS` constant, e.g.: *"Start your reply with a single line `Title: <a concise, specific task title in the imperative, under 80 characters>`, then a blank line, then the plan."*
   - Change the signature to `plan_prompt(task, feedback="", rewrite_title=False)`. When `rewrite_title` is true, add `TITLE_INSTRUCTIONS` right after `PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS`.
   - Add `split_title(text: str) -> tuple[str, str]`, returning `(title, plan)`:
     - Look at the first non-empty line and match it case-insensitively against something like `^\s*[#>*_\s]*title\s*[:\-]\s*(.+?)\s*[*_]*\s*$`, so small markdown variations like `**Title:** …` or `# Title: …` still match.
     - Remove surrounding quotes and backticks from the title, collapse whitespace, and cap it at about 120 characters.
     - Return `("", text)` if there's no match or the title comes out empty.
2. **`patchgoblin/engine.py`**
   - Import `split_title`.
   - In `_plan`, read the setting once with `rewrite = project.get("rewrite_titles", True)` and pass it to `plan_prompt(task, feedback, rewrite_title=rewrite)`.
   - In the `outcome.ok` branch, when `rewrite` is on, call `title, plan = split_title(outcome.text)`. Set `current["plan"] = plan.strip() or outcome.text`.
   - If `title` is non-empty and different from `current["title"]`, set the new title and call `log_event(current, f"Title rewritten by AI (was: {old})")` before `set_status(... "planned" ...)`.
   - Replanning with feedback goes through `_plan` too, so revised plans also get a refreshed title.
3. **`patchgoblin/app.py`**, in `update_project`: accept `"rewrite_titles"` as `fields["rewrite_titles"] = bool(data["rewrite_titles"])`.
   - Optionally, `project_fields` could also accept it so the Add Project dialog can set it. I'd skip that, since the default covers it.

## Plan: make plan questions easy to spot and answer, and make Save/Queue hard to mis-click

**Summary.** Today the planner's questions sit at the bottom of the free-text plan under "open questions or risks", so they're easy to miss. The only way to reply is the general "Feedback for AI planning" box. In the drawer, Save sits right next to Queue for AI and Delete, and all three look much the same (`renderDrawer` in `app.js`). The fix has two parts. First, ask the planner to put its questions in a fixed `## Questions for you` section. The server reads that section out of the plan, and the UI shows the questions in a highlighted panel above the plan, each with its own answer box and one "Answer & refine plan" button. Cards also get a "N questions" badge so they stand out on the board. Second, split the drawer buttons into separate groups. Save only appears when there are unsaved edits, and it moves next to the form. Workflow buttons get clearer labels and hover text, and Delete moves away from the main buttons. Queueing a task that still has unanswered questions asks for confirmation first.

### Steps

1. **`patchgoblin/providers.py` – planner prompt.** Change `PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS` so the last two bullets become:
   - `## Risks`: things the implementer should watch for.
   - `## Questions for you`: a numbered list of decisions only the user can make. Each question fits on one line. If there are none, the section says `None.`

   Don't change the summary, steps or verification bullets.

2. **`providers.py` – new `plan_questions(plan: str) -> list[str]`.** It finds a heading matching `^#{1,6}\s*(open\s+)?questions\b` (case-insensitive) and collects the numbered or bulleted items up to the next heading. Wrapped continuation lines join onto the item above. Items like "None" are dropped. It is a pure function, so it's easy to test, and it also reads plans made before this change that use an "Open questions" heading.

3. **`providers.py` – `plan_prompt(task, feedback="", answers=None)`.** When `answers` (a list of `{question, answer}` pairs) is given, add a `## Answers to your questions` section listing each Q and A. Skip blank answers. Then tell the planner to fold the answers into a complete revised plan and to repeat only questions that are still open. Keep the existing feedback section.

4. **`patchgoblin/app.py` – `task_view`.** Add `"questions": plan_questions(task.get("plan", ""))`. Working this out from the plan on every request keeps it correct after manual edits, with nothing extra saved in tasks.json. In `task_action`, pass `data.get("answers")` into `engine.start_planning`, after checking that it's a list of dicts with string fields.

5. **`patchgoblin/engine.py` – `start_planning` / `_plan`.** Accept `answers` and pass it on to `plan_prompt`. The history message becomes "AI planning started with answers/feedback" when either one is present.

6. **`patchgoblin/templates/index.html` – drawer layout.**
   - Add a `<section id="d-questions" class="questions" hidden>` above the Plan label. It holds a heading ("The AI has questions for you"), an `<ol id="d-question-list">` and a primary "Answer & refine plan" button.
   - Put the Plan textarea inside a `<details open>`-style block, or give it a smaller default `rows`, so the questions show without scrolling.
   - Split `#d-actions` into three rows:
     - `#d-edit-actions`, right under the form fields: "Save changes" and "Discard".
     - `#d-flow-actions`: the workflow buttons.
     - `#d-danger-actions`: Delete, pushed right, or into the drawer header.
   - Rename the feedback label to "Other feedback for the AI (optional)".

7. **`patchgoblin/static/app.js`.**
   - **`renderDrawer`:** fill `#d-question-list` from `t.questions`. Each item shows the question text plus a one-line textarea (`data-q` index). Show the panel only when `canPlan && t.questions.length`. Keep typed answers across the 3-second poll re-renders: only rebuild when the questions change, using a stamp like `formStamp`.
   - **New `answerQuestions()`:** collect the answers and call `doAction("plan", { answers })`. If no answer is filled in, show a toast and stop.
   - **`doAction(action, extra)`:** it already takes the `extra` argument, but the current code doesn't use it. Merge `extra` into `body`, and clear the answer boxes after a successful plan.
   - **Buttons:**
     - Show Save only when `state.dirty`. The `input` listeners call a light `renderEditActions()` so the button appears as soon as the user types, plus an "Unsaved changes" hint.
     - Relabel "Queue for AI" to "Queue to run", with the hover text "The AI will implement this plan and commit the result".
     - Change "Mark planned" to "Mark planned (skip AI)".
     - If `t.questions.length` > 0, queueing asks `confirm("The plan still has N unanswered questions. Queue anyway?")`.
     - Delete stays behind its existing confirm, but moves out of the main button row.
   - **`renderCard`:** add a `chip` reading `? N questions` when `t.questions.length` is above 0 and the task is `planned`/`unplanned`/`failed`.
   - **Ctrl+S:** keep it, since saving through it is intentional.

8. **`patchgoblin/static/app.css`.**
   - Style `.questions` with an accent border and background so it stands out, plus a `.chip.question` colour.
   - Separate the edit, workflow and delete rows with spacing or a divider, and align the danger row to the right.

### Verification
- **Unit tests** in `tests/test_patchgoblin.py`:
  - `plan_questions`: covers the new heading, the older "Open questions" heading, "None.", wrapped items, and no section at all.
  - `plan_prompt` with answers: the section is included and blank answers are skipped.
  - API: `GET /tasks` returns `questions` for a task whose plan contains the section, and `POST .../action {"action":"plan","answers":[...]}` is accepted (use `tests/fake_agent.py` and extend it to print a plan with questions). Also check that badly formed `answers` returns 400.
- **Existing tests:** run the whole suite with `python -m pytest` or `uv run pytest`; `test_plan_queue_run_commit` and `test_manual_plan_and_failed_run` should still pass.
- **Manual check in the running app (`run.py`):**
  1. Plan a task and check that the questions panel and the card badge appear.
  2. Type an answer, wait more than 3 seconds for the poll refresh, and check the answer is still there.
  3. Click "Answer & refine plan" and check the prompt in the live output includes the answers.
  4. Check that Save only appears after editing.
  5. Check that queueing with open questions asks for confirmation.
  6. Check that Delete is visually separate from the other buttons.

### Open questions and risks
- **Output format.** Models may not follow the section format exactly. The parser should be lenient, and if it finds nothing the plan still displays as it does now.
- **Manual plans.** If the user writes their own plan with a "Questions" heading, it will trigger the panel. That's probably what they'd want.
- **Blocking the queue.** Should unanswered questions block queueing outright? This plan only asks for confirmation.
- **Save placement.** Is hiding Save until there are edits enough, or should the form save automatically when the drawer closes, removing the button entirely? This plan keeps a Save button to limit the scope.
- **Queue auto-save.** Queueing already saves pending edits automatically. That will now be visible as "Save & queue" behaviour, so the button label or hover text should say so.

tasks.description: add option to sync up with a remote git repository.
tasks.plan:
## Summary
PatchGoblin makes each project its own git repo and commits every finished task, but it never talks to a remote. `gitops.py` even says "Nothing is ever pushed". This plan adds remote sync with one remote, `origin`, built from existing pieces:
- **New `gitops` helpers** to read and set the remote, report ahead/behind status, and run a safe sync: checkpoint-commit, `fetch`, `pull --ff-only` (or `--rebase`), then `push -u`.
- **Three API routes** under `/api/projects/<pid>/remote`.
- **UI:** a "Sync" button and a Remote dialog, next to the existing project toolbar buttons.

**Manual sync:**
- It always commits dirty files, including `tasks.json`, before pulling.
- It is refused while any AI job or chat for the project is running.
- Conflicts or diverged history are aborted and reported. It never creates merge commits.

**Auto-sync (per-project setting, default off):**
- It is a new `auto_sync` project field, stored and edited like `rewrite_titles`.
- When on, `Engine._execute` runs a sync after a task's successful commit.
- It still pushes if there's nothing new to pull.
- A failed auto-sync is written to the task's event log and never marks the task as failed.

**Other behaviour:**
- Credentials come from the user's own git setup, and prompts are turned off so a missing credential fails fast.
- Errors come back as `HostError`, which the existing handler turns into a readable 502.
- It works for both local and SSH projects because every command goes through `host.run`.

## Steps

1. **`patchgoblin/gitops.py`**
   - Change the module docstring: pushing happens only through an explicit sync, either manual or per-project auto-sync.
   - Add `NOPROMPT` handling. Run remote commands as `git -c credential.interactive=never ...` with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` set. Check whether `host.run` accepts `env`. If it doesn't, add an optional `env` parameter to both host classes in `patchgoblin/hosts.py`. For SSH, prefix the command with `env GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and quote it the same way as the existing command building.
   - `get_remote(host, path, name="origin") -> str`: runs `git remote get-url`. Returns `""` if there is no remote.
   - `set_remote(host, path, url, name="origin")`:
     - Strips `url`. An empty `url` runs `git remote remove`, and a missing remote is not an error.
     - Rejects a URL that starts with `-` or contains whitespace or newlines, by raising `ValueError`.
     - Otherwise runs `set-url` if the remote exists, or `add` if it doesn't.
   - `current_branch(host, path)`: runs `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`. Raises `HostError("detached HEAD; cannot sync")` if HEAD is detached.
   - `remote_status(host, path) -> dict`: returns `{url, branch, upstream, ahead, behind, dirty}`.
     - `ahead`/`behind` come from `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{u}`, only if an upstream is set.
     - If there's no upstream but a remote exists, report `ahead` as the local commit count.
     - It never fetches.
   - `sync(host, path, mode="ff-only", push=True, checkpoint=True) -> dict`:
     1. If `get_remote` is empty, raise `HostError("no remote configured")`.
     2. Get `branch = current_branch(...)`.
     3. If `checkpoint` is true and `has_changes(host, path)`, run `commit_all(host, path, "PatchGoblin: checkpoint before sync")`.
     4. Run `git fetch origin`.
     5. If `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <branch>` finds the branch:
        - ff-only: `git pull --ff-only --autostash origin <branch>`
        - rebase: `git pull --rebase --autostash origin <branch>`
        - If the rebase fails, run `git rebase --abort` (ignore any error from it), then raise `HostError` with git's stderr.
     6. If `push` is true: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
     7. Return `{"log": [...short step lines...], **remote_status(...)}`.
   - Use a longer timeout than the default for fetch, pull and push. The existing 300 s `git()` timeout is acceptable.
   - Mode is validated by the caller. Accept only `"ff-only"` and `"rebase"`.

2. **`patchgoblin/engine.py`**
   - Add a per-project sync lock, `self._sync_locks: dict[pid, threading.Lock]`, created under `self._lock`. Both manual and auto-sync hold it, so they never overlap.
   - Add `def busy(self, pid) -> bool`. It returns `any(k[0] == pid for k in self.jobs) or self.chat(pid).job is not None`. Use it in `app.py`'s `remove_project`, replacing the inline check.
   - Add `def sync(self, project, mode, push, checkpoint=True)`. It takes the lock (non-blocking; if the lock is held, raise `ValueError("sync already in progress")`), calls `gitops.sync`, then calls `self.store.forget(project["id"])` or the equivalent, so a `tasks.json` changed by the pull gets reloaded.
   - In `_execute`, after the block at lines 318–325 that records `commit`, if `outcome.ok and project.get("auto_sync") is True`:
     - Call `gitops.sync(host, path, mode=project.get("sync_mode", "ff-only"), push=True, checkpoint=True)` under the project's sync lock.
     - `checkpoint=True` is needed because recording the commit SHA just made `tasks.json` dirty again. The result is one small extra checkpoint commit. It's acceptable, but see Risks.
     - Wrap the call in `try/except HostError`. On success, `log_event(current, "Synced with origin")`. On failure, `log_event(current, f"Auto-sync failed: {exc}")`. Never change the task's status.
     - Write a line to `job` as well, so it shows in the live output.
   - Skip auto-sync if no remote is configured, so the event log isn't spammed.
   - Auto-sync runs inside the task's own job, so it must not call `busy()`, because it would reject itself.

3. **`patchgoblin/app.py`** (next to the `commits`/`terminal` routes)
   - `GET /api/projects/<pid>/remote` returns `gitops.remote_status(...)` plus `auto_sync` and `sync_mode` from the project.
   - `PUT /api/projects/<pid>/remote` with body `{url}` calls `set_remote`, then returns the status.
   - `POST /api/projects/<pid>/remote/sync` with body `{mode, push}`:
     - Checks `mode` is `"ff-only"` or `"rebase"`.
     - Rejects with `ValueError` if `engine.busy(pid)` or any task in `store.read(project)` has status `planning` or `running`.
     - Calls `engine.sync(project, mode, push)` and returns the result.
   - In `update_project` (around line 162), accept `auto_sync` (bool) and `sync_mode` (`"ff-only"` or `"rebase"`), following the `rewrite_titles` pattern.

4. **`patchgoblin/store.py`**: confirm that `forget(pid)`, or an equivalent, drops any cached `tasks.json` so the next `read` reloads it from disk. Only add a helper if nothing like that exists.

5. **`patchgoblin/templates/index.html`**
   - Beside the `#p-rewrite-titles` label (around line 51), add:
     ```html
     <label class="check" title="After each successful task commit, pull and push to origin">
       <input type="checkbox" id="p-auto-sync"> Auto-sync
     </label>
     ```
   - Add `<button class="ghost" id="sync-btn">Sync</button>` near `#commits-btn`.
   - Add `<dialog id="remote-dialog">`, built like `#commits-dialog`, containing:
     - a remote URL input with a Save button
     - a status line (branch, upstream, ahead/behind, dirty)
     - a mode select (fast-forward only / rebase), which also saves `sync_mode`
     - a "push after pull" checkbox, checked by default
     - a "Sync now" button, a log/error area, and a Close button

6. **`patchgoblin/static/app.js`**
   - In the project render (around line 157), add `$("#p-auto-sync").checked = p.auto_sync === true;`.
   - Add a change handler that mirrors the one at line 951: `updateProject({ auto_sync: e.target.checked })`.
   - Add `showRemote()`: calls `GET /remote`, fills the dialog and opens it.
   - Save calls `PUT /remote`.
   - The mode select calls `updateProject({ sync_mode })`.
   - "Sync now" calls `POST /remote/sync`. While it runs, disable the button and show "Syncing…". Afterwards, show `toast("Synced")` or the error, show the returned log, and refresh the tasks and status.
   - Wire `#sync-btn` in `init()` the same way as `#commits-btn`.
   - Optionally disable the Auto-sync checkbox, with a tooltip, when no remote is set. This is cosmetic only; the server skips sync anyway.

7. **`patchgoblin/static/app.css`**: minor styling for the status line and log `<pre>`, if needed.

8. **`README.md`**: document:
   - remote setup
   - manual sync behaviour (checkpoint commit, ff-only or rebase, abort on conflict)
   - the Auto-sync project toggle (default off)
   - that credentials come from the user's own git, SSH or credential-manager setup

## Verification
- Add tests to `tests/test_patchgoblin.py`. Use a temp `git init --bare` repo as `origin`, and set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
  - `test_remote_set_and_status`: PUT the URL, then GET returns the URL and branch, and `ahead` is at least 1.
  - `test_set_remote_rejects_option_like_url`: a URL starting with `-` returns 400.
  - `test_sync_pushes_to_empty_remote`: after sync, `git rev-parse <branch>` in the bare repo equals the project's HEAD.
  - `test_sync_commits_dirty_tree_first`: with an uncommitted file present, sync leaves a "checkpoint before sync" commit, and that commit has been pushed.
  - `test_sync_pulls_fast_forward`: commit and push from a clone, then sync the project; the project gets the commit.
  - `test_sync_diverged_ff_only_fails_cleanly`: returns a 502 with git's message, and `git status` shows no merge or rebase in progress.
  - `test_sync_rebase_mode`: after a diverged sync, the history is linear, and the remote contains both commits.
  - `test_sync_rejected_while_busy`: with a fake entry in `engine.jobs`, returns 400.
  - `test_auto_sync_off_by_default`: run a task with `fake_agent.py`; the bare repo stays empty.
  - `test_auto_sync_pushes_after_task`: set `auto_sync` to true and run a task; the bare repo has the task commit, and the task log contains "Synced with origin".
  - `test_auto_sync_failure_does_not_fail_task`: point the remote at a bogus path; the task is still `done`, and the log contains "Auto-sync failed".
  - `test_update_project_auto_sync_field`: PUT `auto_sync` and `sync_mode` round-trip; an invalid `sync_mode` is rejected.
- Run `uv run python -m unittest discover tests` (or pytest). All existing tests must still pass.
- Manual checks with `uv run run.py`:
  - Set a GitHub remote, sync, edit on GitHub, then sync again.
  - Turn on Auto-sync, run a task, and confirm the push.
  - Repeat on an SSH project.

## Risks
- **Extra commits with auto-sync:** writing the commit SHA into `tasks.json` after the task commit makes the tree dirty again. Each auto-sync then adds a "checkpoint before sync" commit. To avoid that, the implementer could record the SHA first and amend, or pass `checkpoint=False` and rely on `--autostash`. Watch that `--autostash` doesn't leave stash entries behind if a pull fails.
- **Hanging credential prompts:** an SSH `ssh-askpass` or a Windows GCM GUI prompt can still block despite `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. Consider adding `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` when it isn't already set.
- **Blocking during sync:** a manual sync blocks a Flask request thread for up to the git timeout. An auto-sync extends the task's job, so the project shows as busy until the push finishes.
- **Queued tasks and `tasks.json`:** a pull can replace `tasks.json` while other tasks are queued. After every sync, reload the store (`forget`). The engine must re-read the doc and not reuse a stale `project`/`doc` object. Task ID collisions between machines are accepted.
- **Rebase mode:** a failed rebase must always be aborted, otherwise the repo is left mid-rebase and later task runs break. Test this path.
- **URLs with credentials:** a URL like `https://token@...` would be stored in `.git/config` and shown in the UI. Don't log the URL in task events; just say "origin".
- **Detached HEAD or no branch:** a detached HEAD, or a fresh repo with no commits, must give a clear error, not a traceback.
- **SSH env quoting:** the `env` prefix on SSH commands has to use the same quoting helper as the rest of `hosts.py`.

## Questions for you
None.

The single project `model` field is split into **`plan_model`** and **`code_model`**, shown in the UI as "Planning Model" and "Coding Model". A single resolver, `Engine.provider_for(project, task, role)`, picks the model in this order: **task override → project setting (chat: `chat_model` → `plan_model`) → global default for that provider and role → the CLI's or endpoint's own default**. The existing rule stays: project models only apply when the task uses the project's provider. Task models always go with the task's effective provider. # Task #11 plan: add a Review step between the AI finishing a run and the task counting as finished

## Summary
Add a new task status, `review`, between `running` and `done`. When an AI run succeeds, `Engine._execute` will set the task to `review` instead of `done`. The commit still happens automatically, as it does now. Tasks in `review` get their own "Review" tab on the board, placed between "AI queue" and "Finished". From there the engineer can **Approve**, which moves the task to `done` (Finished), or **Send back**, which returns it to `planned` so it can be revised and queued again. Both are ordinary entries in the `TRANSITIONS` table in `app.py`, so single-task and batch actions work with no new endpoints. Failed runs still go straight to `failed`, because there is nothing to validate. Tasks already marked `done` stay as they are, so no data migration is needed.

## Steps
1. **`patchgoblin/store.py`**: Add `"review"` to `STATUSES` between `"running"` and `"done"`. `set_status` asserts against this tuple, so this has to come first.
2. **`patchgoblin/engine.py` → `Engine._execute`**: On success, replace `set_status(current, "done", "AI run finished")` with `set_status(current, "review", "AI run finished; awaiting review")`. Leave the failure path and the commit step as they are. Update the module docstring if it mentions `done`.
3. **`patchgoblin/app.py` → `TRANSITIONS`**:
   - Add `"approve": (("review",), "done", "Approved by engineer")`.
   - Add `"send_back": (("review",), "planned", "Sent back after review")`.
   - Keep `"reopen"` from `done`. Consider also allowing `reopen` from `review`, or let `send_back` cover that case.
   - Leave `LOCKED` alone, because `review` tasks should stay editable and deletable. `BATCH_ACTIONS` picks up the new actions automatically since it is built from `TRANSITIONS`.
4. **`patchgoblin/templates/index.html`**: Add `("review", "Review")` to the tab list at line 62 and `"review"` to the column list at line 69. Both go between `queue` and `finished`.
5. **`patchgoblin/static/app.js`**:
   - `STATUS_LABEL`: add `review: "Needs review"`.
   - `COLUMN_OF`: add `review: "review"`.
   - `ACTIONABLE`: add `"review"` so the tab badge counts tasks waiting for the engineer. Update the comment that says it mirrors `LOCKED`.
   - `sortTasks`: sort the `review` column by `finished_at`, oldest first, so the longest-waiting task is on top.
   - `renderDrawer`: add a `case "review":` with a primary "Approve → Finished" button (`act("approve")`) and a ghost "Send back to planned" button (`act("send_back")`). Show the commit hash, which already works through `#d-commit`, so the engineer knows what to check.
   - If there is a batch toolbar that lists actions per column (search for the `batch` usage below line 420), add Approve there for the review column.
6. **`patchgoblin/static/app.css`**: Add `.badge.review` with new `--b-review` and `--t-review` variables. Define them in both the light and dark theme blocks, next to the existing `--b-done` and `--t-done`.
7. **`README.md`**: In the status table near line 45, add a "Needs review" row. Change the Done row to say it means approved by the engineer.
8. **`tests/test_patchgoblin.py`**:
   - `test_plan_queue_run_commit`: wait for `{"review", "failed"}` and assert `review`. Check that the commit still exists. Then call `approve` and assert `done`. Also update the `stored["status"]` check.
   - Add `test_review_actions`: `approve` and `send_back` work only from `review`, and both return 400 from any other status. `send_back` lands in `planned`. The batch `approve` works on several tasks.
   - Make sure `reopen` still works from `done`.

## Verification
- Run `python -m pytest tests -q`. All tests should pass, including the updated and new ones.
- Manual check: run the app, queue a task, and confirm it shows up under the Review tab with an actionable count badge and its commit hash. Approve it and confirm it moves to Finished. Queue another task, send it back, and confirm it moves to Planned with history entries logged.
- Confirm that an existing `.patchgoblin/tasks.json` with `done` tasks still loads and renders.

## Risks

I read your "yes" on Q1 as keeping the label "Drafted". A drafted task leaves the tab in one of four ways:

# Plan: Task #13: support multiple named OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, …)

Right now there is a single hard-wired `openai` provider. Its key can only come from `OPENAI_API_KEY`. It has one base URL and a fixed model list, and its reply parsing assumes api.openai.com behaviour. This plan replaces it with a list of **endpoints** stored in settings. Each endpoint has:
- a stable id and a display name chosen by the user
- a base URL
- an API key, either saved or read from an env var. **The saved key wins when both are set.**
- optional extra headers
- a default model, manual model suggestions, max steps and allow-commands

Each endpoint appears as its own provider, by name, in every AI dropdown. Existing data keeps working: the old `openai` settings block becomes an endpoint with id `openai`, so projects and tasks that store `provider: "openai"` don't change. An endpoint's model dropdown combines its manual suggestions with a live list from `{base_url}/models`. That list is fetched through a new server route and cached briefly. The agent loop also becomes more tolerant of replies from compatible servers. An endpoint that projects or tasks still use can be removed after a confirmation. Those references then fail with a clear "provider missing" error.

## Steps

1. **`patchgoblin/store.py`: endpoint settings model**

     - Raise a clear error if the result is empty or not `http(s)://`.
   - **Add `endpoint_headers(ep)`:**
     - Start from the user's headers, dropping any whose name or value contains CR/LF.

     - Take the endpoint dict and use the helpers above in `_request`.

       - there is no key,
       - the host is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`,
       - and `api_key_env` or a saved key was configured.
     - The message is: "`<ENV>` is not set in PatchGoblin's environment and no key is saved for <name>."
     - Endpoints with no key settings at all are treated as intentionally keyless.
     - Use neutral wording when the model is missing: "No model configured for <name>."
   - **Reply parsing:**
     - If the reply has an `error` key, or `choices` is missing or empty, return `Outcome(False, error=…)`.
     - Echo back only `role` (always `"assistant"`), `content` and `tool_calls`, not the whole message.
     - Accept `function.arguments` as a dict or a JSON string, and treat `""` as `{}`.
     - If a tool call has no `id`, assign `call_{step}_{i}` and write it into the echoed `tool_calls` so that `tool_call_id` matches.
     - The job log line becomes `"<name> agent: model …"`.

3. **`patchgoblin/app.py`**

     - Pass `providers=provider_choices(settings.get())`.
     - Pass `models` with claude and codex from `MODELS`, plus each endpoint's `models` suggestions. The endpoint with id `openai` also gets the built-in OpenAI list.
   - **`get_settings`:**
     - Return settings with each endpoint's `api_key` **blanked**.

     - Remove `openai_key_present`.
   - **`put_settings`:** accept `"endpoints"` and validate each one:
     - The id is a slug (`[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}`), unique, and not `claude` or `codex`. A new endpoint without an id gets one made from its name, de-duplicated.
     - The name is not empty.
     - The base URL is http(s).
     - `max_steps` is between 1 and 200.
     - Header names and values are strings with no CR/LF.
   - **Keys in `put_settings`:**
     - An empty `api_key` keeps the saved key for that id.
     - `"api_key_clear": true` removes the saved key.
     - The key is never echoed back.
   - Stop accepting the top-level `"openai"` key.
   - Return the updated `providers` and `models` in the response so the client can rebuild its selects.
   - **Provider validation:** replace every `in PROVIDERS` check with `valid_provider(settings.get(), …)`. That covers `project_fields`, `update_project`, task create, task edit and the `set_provider` batch action. An empty `""` stays allowed for tasks. Grep afterwards so none are missed.
   - **New route `GET /api/endpoints/<eid>/models`:**
     - It calls `list_models`, with an in-memory cache keyed by id + base_url + key presence, for about 10 minutes. `?refresh=1` skips the cache.
     - It returns `{"models": [...], "error": ""}`. On failure it still returns 200, with `error` set and only the manual suggestions.
   - **New route `POST /api/endpoints/test`:** takes an unsaved endpoint from the form. If the key field is blank, it uses the saved key for that id. It runs `list_models` and returns the model count or the error.

4. **`patchgoblin/templates/index.html`**
   - **Provider selects:** render all four (`#p-provider`, `#batch-provider`, `#d-provider`, new-project `provider`) as `{% for p in providers %}<option value="{{ p.id }}">{{ p.name }}</option>`. Give them a shared class (e.g. `provider-select`) so JS can rebuild them.
   - Put `data-providers` / `data-models` JSON on `<body>`, or extend the existing data block.
   - **Settings fieldset:** replace the "OpenAI API" fieldset with "OpenAI-compatible APIs". It contains an `#endpoint-list` container, an "Add endpoint" button, and a `<template id="endpoint-tpl">` with these fields:
     - Name
     - Base URL, placeholder `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`
     - API key (`type=password`, placeholder "saved" or "not set", plus a Clear checkbox)
     - Key env var
     - Default model
     - Model suggestions
     - Extra headers textarea, one `Name: value` per line
     - Max steps
     - Allow commands
     - Test and Remove buttons, and a status span
   - **Hint text:** "A saved key takes priority over the env var. Saved keys are stored in plain text in PatchGoblin's settings.json."

5. **`patchgoblin/static/app.js`**
   - Keep `SETTING_FIELDS` for claude, codex and timeouts. Remove the `openai.*` entries.
   - **`renderEndpoints(list)` / `readEndpoints()`:**
     - Clone the template for each endpoint and keep `id` in `data-id`.
     - Convert `models` between a list and space/comma-separated text.
     - Convert `headers` between a dict and `Name: value` lines, ignoring blank lines and lines without `:`.

   - **Buttons:**
     - "Add endpoint" appends an empty block.
     - "Remove" first checks `state.projects` (and loaded tasks) for that id. If any use it, call `confirm("N project(s)/task(s) use <name>; they will fail with 'provider missing' until changed. Remove anyway?")`. Remove only if confirmed.
     - "Test" POSTs to `/api/endpoints/test` and shows the model count or the error.
   - **Saving:**
     - Send `{commands, timeouts, endpoints}`.
     - On success, update `PROVIDERS` and `MODELS` from the response, call a new `renderProviderSelects()`, and clear the models cache.
     - `renderProviderSelects()` rebuilds all `.provider-select` elements and keeps each current value. If a value no longer exists, add a disabled-looking option `"<id> (missing)"` so the stale value stays visible instead of silently switching to claude.
   - **Display names:** add `providerName(id)`, which falls back to `"<id> (missing)"`. Use it in the task chip (~line 279) and `#c-where` (~line 677).
   - **Loading models:** add `async ensureModels(provider)`.
     - For endpoint providers, fetch `/api/endpoints/<id>/models` once per session.
     - Merge the result into `MODELS[provider]`, suggestions first, deduplicated.
     - Show a "Loading models…" option while fetching, and put any error in a `title` or muted option.
   - **Where to call `ensureModels`:**
     - When the project view opens (~line 154).

6. **`patchgoblin/engine.py`**
   - Confirm that `provider_for` only compares ids.
   - Confirm that `plan_questions` and chat go through `run_ai`.
   - Grep the repo for leftover `"openai"` literals and `PROVIDERS` uses.

7. **`README.md`:** replace the "OpenAI API" bullet with an "OpenAI-compatible endpoints" section. It should cover:
   - You can have several named endpoints.
   - The key is either saved (it takes priority, and is stored in plain text in settings.json) or read from an env var.
   - Models are listed from `/models`, and they must support tool calling.
   - Removing an endpoint that is in use leaves those projects and tasks with a "provider missing" error until you reassign them.
   - Examples:
     - OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY`)
     - OpenRouter (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`)
     - Ollama or LM Studio with no key (`http://localhost:11434/v1`)

8. **`tests/test_patchgoblin.py`**
   - **`OpenAIAgentTests`** (patch `urllib.request.urlopen`):
     - The saved `api_key` is used, and it wins over a set `api_key_env`. The env var is used when no key is saved.
     - No `Authorization` header is sent when there is no key.
     - Extra headers are sent, headers containing CR/LF are dropped, and the configured key overrides a user `Authorization` header.
     - The base URL variants `…/v1/`, `…/v1/chat/completions` and ` …/v1 ` all resolve to `…/v1/chat/completions`.
     - A 200 reply containing `{"error": …}`, or with no `choices`, gives a failed `Outcome` with the message.
     - A tool call with no `id` and dict `arguments` still runs, and the `tool_call_id` matches.
     - Extra fields such as `reasoning` are removed from the echoed history.
     - A missing key on a non-local host with `api_key_env` set fails early and names the env var.
   - **`list_models`:** it parses the OpenAI shape, filters by `supported_parameters`, and raises on HTTP errors.
   - **Settings:** a legacy file containing only an `"openai"` block migrates to endpoint `openai` with its old base_url and model. `run_ai("openai", …)` routes to the agent. `run_ai("deleted-id", …)` returns the "not configured" error.
   - **App routes:**
     - A PUT with two endpoints saves both.
     - A duplicate id, or the id `claude`, is rejected.
     - GET blanks `api_key` and reports `api_key_saved`.
     - A PUT with a blank key keeps the saved key, and `api_key_clear` removes it.
     - A project or task can be set to a new endpoint id, and an unknown id returns 400.
     - The `/api/endpoints/<id>/models` route works with `list_models` patched, and its cache and `refresh` behave as described.

## Verification

- Run `python -m unittest tests.test_patchgoblin -v`. All existing and new tests should pass.
- **Migration:** start the app with the current settings.json. There should be one "OpenAI" endpoint, and existing `openai` projects should still show up and run.
- **OpenRouter:**
  1. Add "OpenRouter" (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`), paste a key and click Test. It should show a model count.
  2. Save. It should appear in all four dropdowns without reloading.
  3. Pick it for a project. The model dropdown should fill from `/models`. Choose `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
  4. Plan a task, then run a task that writes a file.
- **Key priority:** set both a saved key and an env var that holds an invalid key. Test should succeed, which shows the saved key was used.
- **Two endpoints:** set the project to one endpoint and a single task to the other. The job logs should show the right endpoint name and model for each.
- **Local server:** add a keyless endpoint at `http://localhost:11434/v1`. The models should load and planning should work.
- **Removal:** remove an endpoint that a project uses. A confirm dialog should appear. After you accept:
  - the project's select shows "<id> (missing)",
  - running a task fails with the "not configured" error,
  - reassigning the provider fixes it.
- **No key leak:** check in devtools that GET `/api/settings` never contains a saved key.

## Risks

- **ID stability:** projects and tasks store endpoint ids, so renaming an endpoint must change only `name`. Removal is allowed after a confirmation, so stale references are expected. The UI and `run_ai` must show them clearly and must never silently fall back to claude.
- **Plain-text secrets:**
  - Never send a saved key to the browser.
  - A blank key field means "keep the saved key".
  - Keep keys out of logs and error text.
  - Confirm settings.json lives in the app data dir, not in `.patchgoblin/`, so it can never be committed. This matters because remote git sync (task #7) now exists.
- **`_merge` replaces lists:** the endpoints list must go through `save_endpoints`. Otherwise partial client data could wipe endpoints.
- **The `/models` endpoint:** it can be large (OpenRouter), missing, or require auth. Filter by tool support, cache results, fall back to manual suggestions, and never block rendering on the fetch.
- **Model dropdown race:** await `ensureModels` before `modelFor`, so a valid custom model isn't dropped.
- **Header injection:** reject CR/LF in headers. The configured key's `Authorization` header must win.
- **Keyless heuristic:** a remote endpoint with a misconfigured env var and no saved key fails early, which is intended. Remote servers that truly need no auth must have no key and no env var configured.
- **Tool-calling support:** many models reject `tools`, for example OpenRouter's 404 "No endpoints found that support tool use". That message must reach the task error.
- **Removing reasoning fields from echoed history:** this helps compatibility but may slightly weaken multi-turn reasoning on some models.
- **Provider validation is spread out:** it lives in five places in `app.py`, and missing one leaves a 400 "Unknown provider" for new endpoints.

## Questions for you

None.

tasks.title: Close the task drawer and chat panel when clicking outside them
tasks.plan:
The task drawer and the chat panel will both close when you click outside them, and there will be no docked tab. One `pointerdown` listener on `document`, registered in `init()` in `patchgoblin/static/app.js`, handles both panels. For the task drawer (`#drawer`), an outside press calls the existing `closeDrawer()`, which keeps the "Discard unsaved changes?" confirm. Presses on task cards are skipped, so `openDrawer(tid)` still switches tasks. For the chat panel (`#chat`), an outside press calls the existing `closeChat()`, the same full close used by ✕ and Escape. Closing chat is safe:
- `closeChat()` only hides the panel and stops polling.
- The conversation is stored on the server, and `loadChat()` fetches it again when chat reopens.
- `#c-input` is never cleared, so a half-typed message is still there when you reopen chat with `#chat-btn`.

Opening a task while chat is open still closes chat, because `openDrawer()` already calls `closeChat()`. Escape stays a full close. The listener uses `pointerdown` instead of `click` because a card's click handler calls `renderBoard()`. That replaces the element under the pointer before a document-level `click` handler would see it.

## Steps

1. **`app.js`: add a helper near `closeDrawer()` (~line 507):**
   ```js
   // A press counts as "outside" a panel unless it lands in it, in an open dialog, or on the toast.
   function isOutside(panel, target) {
     return target.isConnected && !panel.contains(target) && !target.closest("dialog[open], #toast");
   }
   ```
2. **`app.js`, `init()`: add a `pointerdown` listener right after the `data-close` click listener (line 1224):**
   ```js
   document.addEventListener("pointerdown", e => {
     if (e.button !== 0 || document.querySelector("dialog[open]")) return;
     const drawer = $("#drawer"), chatPanel = $("#chat");
     if (!drawer.hidden && isOutside(drawer, e.target)
         && !e.target.closest(".card[data-tid], #chat-btn") && !closeDrawer()) {
       e.preventDefault();
       e.stopPropagation();
     }
     if (!chatPanel.hidden && isOutside(chatPanel, e.target) && !e.target.closest("#chat-btn")) closeChat();
   });
   ```
   - **Card presses:** `openDrawer()` handles these itself, including its own unsaved-changes confirm.
   - **`#chat-btn` presses:** these are skipped for both panels. For the drawer, `openChat()` already calls `closeDrawer()`, so skipping it here avoids asking the confirm twice. For chat, skipping it stops the button from closing chat on `pointerdown` and reopening it on `click`.
   - **Chat close:** the press is not cancelled, so a click on a card still opens that task after chat closes.
3. **No changes needed to:**
   - `openChat`, `closeChat`, `loadChat`, `openDrawer`, the Escape handler (line 1236), `index.html` or `app.css`.
   - The `chat` state object. It needs no new fields.
4. **Optional cleanup:** add a one-line comment above the listener explaining why it uses `pointerdown`, matching the short comment style used elsewhere in the file.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest` should still pass. This change is frontend-only.
- Manual checks in the running app (`/run`):
  1. **Task drawer:** open a task, then click empty board space, the project sidebar or the header. The drawer closes.
  2. **Switching tasks:** open task A, then click card B. The drawer switches to B and stays open.
  3. **Unsaved edits:** edit a task's title, then click outside the drawer. The confirm appears. Cancel keeps the drawer open with the edits, and the click does nothing else. OK closes the drawer.
  4. **Unsaved edits, then chat button:** click `#chat-btn`. There is exactly one confirm, and chat opens only if you choose OK.
  5. **Batch select:** tick a card's checkbox while the drawer is open. The checkbox toggles and the drawer stays open.
  6. **Presses that must not close anything:**
     - inputs and buttons inside the drawer
     - a text selection dragged from inside the drawer to outside it
     - clicks inside an open dialog, such as one opened from the drawer
     - clicks on the toast
     - right-clicks
  7. **Chat outside click:** open chat, type a partial message, then click the board. Chat closes. Click `#chat-btn`. Chat reopens with its history and the draft text.
  8. **Chat mid-reply:** send a message, then click outside while the AI is working. Chat closes. Reopen it after a few seconds: the live output or the finished reply is shown.
  9. **Chat to task:** with chat open, click a card. Chat closes and the task opens in one click.
  10. **Chat button:** clicking `#chat-btn` while chat is open does not flicker it closed. ✕ and Escape still close chat.

## Risks

- **Detached targets:** the 3s `loadTasks` poll and `renderBoard()` replace DOM nodes, so a press can land on a node that has already been removed. The `isConnected` check guards against this. Keep the handler on `pointerdown` rather than `click`.
- **`confirm()` inside `pointerdown`:** `confirm()` blocks the page, and `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` does not suppress the `click` that follows. If Cancel lets the click through, for example onto a batch-bar button or a sidebar project, add a one-shot capture-phase `click` swallow. Test this in Chrome and Firefox.
- **Clicks that also do something else:** a press on the batch bar, the sidebar or another header button now closes the drawer and then performs its own action. Check that batch actions and `selectProject` don't rely on `state.openTid` still being set.
- **Chat reopen cost:** each reopen of chat triggers one immediate `GET /chat`, and the chat poll stops while chat is hidden, which is the current behaviour. A reply that finishes while chat is closed won't be noticed until chat reopens.
- **Touch:** a scroll gesture that starts on the board will close an open panel. If that feels bad, switch to `pointerup` with a small movement threshold.

## Questions for you

None.

tasks.title: Add a per-project planning trust level that controls AI assumptions vs. questions
tasks.plan:
Add a per-project `plan_trust` setting with three levels: `low`, `normal` (the default) and `high`. It changes only the text of the planning prompt. `normal` sends exactly today's `PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS`, so existing projects behave the same. `low` tells the AI to ask about anything ambiguous instead of guessing. `high` tells the AI to use its best judgement on anything the code, the description or common practice can answer, and to ask only when a wrong guess would be costly or hard to undo. At every level the plan keeps its `## Questions for you` section (so `plan_questions()` and the questions dialog keep working). At `low` and `high`, the AI also adds an `## Assumptions` section so the user can still review its guesses. The setting follows the same path as `rewrite_titles`: it is saved in the project registry, updated through `PATCH /api/projects/<pid>`, read in `Engine._plan`, passed to `plan_prompt`, and shown in the project header.

## Steps

1. **`patchgoblin/providers.py`**
   - Add `PLAN_TRUST_LEVELS = ("low", "normal", "high")` and a dict `TRUST_INSTRUCTIONS` holding the extra prompt text for each level. Use `""` for `normal`.
     - `low`: "Planning trust is LOW: do not assume. Whenever the requirements, scope, UX, naming or approach are ambiguous, ask under 'Questions for you' rather than choosing. Prefer asking over guessing."
